bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified geographic presence across India, Europe and other international markets, mitigating single-market dependence
- Dual-brand strategy (Apollo Tyres + Vredestein) spanning mass, premium and luxury price points with growing global brand recognition
- Comprehensive product portfolio across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, off-highway tyres and two-wheelers, positioning it as a full-range Indian tyre manufacturer
- Strong distribution network across key markets enabling deep penetration and last-mile connectivity
- State-of-the-art, highly automated manufacturing facilities across India and Europe supported by a robust global supply chain
- Strong market position in India's commercial vehicle and passenger vehicle segments
- Global, culturally diverse management team supporting execution across markets
- Ongoing R&D investment via dedicated facilities in India, Netherlands and Hungary supporting product innovation
- Long-standing relationships with leading global OEMs and expanding presence in premium OEM segments (e.g. BMW, Mercedes, MG, VinFast fitments)
- Vredestein products consistently top-ranked by independent testing agencies and automotive media in the premium/performance segment
- Brand-building via BCCI/Team India cricket sponsorship enhancing visibility and consumer connect
- Early mover initiatives in electric-vehicle tyre development
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macroeconomic and demand cyclicality across key geographies — Performance is influenced by macroeconomic conditions across geographies; any slowdown in key international markets, particularly Europe and North America, may impact demand and exports, as the tyre industry remains closely linked to overall economic activity.
- Raw material price volatility — Natural rubber prices are subject to agricultural factors while other key inputs (carbon black, synthetic rubber, fabric, chemicals) are influenced by crude oil price movements; these factors may impact cost structures and profitability.
- Foreign exchange volatility — Global operations and dependence on imported raw materials and export markets expose the Company to currency movements that may impact margins and earnings.
- Regulatory change and EV/technology transition — Operates in a dynamic regulatory environment with evolving norms on sustainability, emissions and safety; rapid shifts in market trends, including increasing EV adoption, require continuous adaptation in product development and business strategy.
- Supply chain and geopolitical disruption — Geopolitical developments, disruptions to global logistics, climate-related events and rising input costs may impact supply continuity and increase transportation costs in an increasingly interconnected global environment.
- Competitive intensity — Intense competition from both global and domestic players requires continuous innovation, product differentiation and cost competitiveness to sustain market position.
- Cybersecurity — Growing threats from cyberattacks, including ransomware and phishing attempts, may impact business continuity and data security.
- Human resource dependency — Operations depend on availability of skilled manpower; challenges in talent retention, labour availability and potential labour disruptions may impact manufacturing operations and productivity.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continued focus on strengthening the premium product portfolio, expanding the distribution network and investing in brand building and R&D
- Transformation initiatives aligned with the strategic roadmap, focused on driving operational efficiency, improving product mix and unlocking long-term value
- Dual-brand premiumisation strategy - positioning Vredestein as a premium/luxury brand while Apollo Tyres anchors the mass-premium/OEM segments, across India, Europe and Americas
- Continued expansion into North America to diversify revenue streams
- Strengthening sourcing strategy through supplier collaboration, diversification and onboarding of new suppliers, plus continued sustainable procurement (ISO 20400:2017, GPSNR engagement, INROAD domestic natural-rubber sourcing)
- Development of indigenised, defence-aligned commercial-vehicle tyre products under the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, and introduction of EV-specific tyre patterns across CV and other segments
- Brand building via sponsorship platforms (BCCI/Team India jersey partnership, 'Har Safar Mein Dum Hai' campaign in India, 'Demand a Better Tire' campaign in the Americas)
- Future outlook: continued focus on driving sustainable and profitable growth through disciplined capital allocation and cost optimisation amid an evolving global macro/geopolitical environment
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: No new manufacturing plant or capacity-addition project with a commissioning/ramp timeline is disclosed in this bundle. Expansion activity described is largely commercial/footprint-led: continued distribution-network expansion and brand-building investment in India (Vredestein premiumisation), portfolio expansion in Europe into higher-value UHP/UUHP segments, and continued expansion into North America (dealer-network expansion plus the 'Demand a Better Tire' campaign) as a new avenue for revenue diversification. Product-portfolio expansion during FY26 included the Aspire 5 UHP range and enhanced Amazer 4G Life (PCR), the apterra HT5 highway-terrain tyre (CV/SUV), VIRAT range extensions and steel-breaker Tractor Rear tyres (Farm OHT), and the 16.00-25 Terra MT and Terra G3 (Industrial OHT). The Company also referenced its 'state-of-the-art facility in Andhra Pradesh' as the venue for the FY26 Global Partners' Summit, without describing any new capacity build there.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic tyre demand expected to grow 6-8% during FY26, driven by improving affordability and favourable rural demand conditions
- Replacement segment growth strengthened, particularly in H2FY26, supported by GST rationalisation and improved consumption trends
- OEM demand remained relatively moderate across passenger and commercial vehicle segments, while continued two-wheeler growth supported overall volumes
- Rising radialisation in India's commercial vehicle segment seen as a structural growth opportunity given the Company's TBR brand equity
- Passenger vehicle segment growth expected to continue on rising vehicle parc and increasing demand for premium products
- Two-wheeler segment offers scale-up opportunity on growing market acceptance and favourable demand dynamics
- In Europe, Vredestein's premium positioning, manufacturing footprint and increasing OEM engagements seen as levers to improve product mix and drive replacement demand
- European replacement tyre market (CY25) stayed weak with volumes down across Consumer, TBR and OHT categories; rising imports into EU/UK on lower-cost competition and higher European (energy) production costs are intensifying competitive pressure
- Raw material costs moderated over the first three quarters of FY26 (softer crude-based inputs) before renewed pressure in Q4 from a Brent crude spike (crossing USD 100/barrel) and continued INR depreciation, raising import costs for key inputs
- Global economic outlook for CY26 expected to remain resilient, supported by steady emerging-market performance, while advanced economies see moderate growth; trade policy shifts, energy price volatility and geopolitical developments flagged as swing factors for supply chains, input costs and demand
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Apollo Tyres delivered record Q4 margins (14.6%) and de-leveraged to 0.4x net debt/EBITDA, but faces immediate margin compression in FY27 due to a mid-to-high teens raw material cost spike requiring multiple price hikes. The strategic closure of the Enschede plant sets the stage for European margin recovery in H2FY27, while India operations remain volume-driven despite inflationary headwinds.
